dhp256:2: To pass judgment hurriedly doesn’t mean you’re a judge. The wise one, weighing both the right judgment & wrong,
dhp257:3: unhurriedly, in line with the Dhamma, guarding the Dhamma, guarded by Dhamma, intelligent:
dhp258:2: Simply talking a lot doesn’t mean one is wise.
dhp259:3: doesn’t maintain the Dhamma. Whoever –although he’s heard next to nothing–
dhp259:6: he’s one who maintains the Dhamma.
dhp260:2: A head of gray hairs doesn’t mean one’s an elder. Advanced in years,
dhp261:1: But one in whom there is truth,
dhp261:2: restraint, rectitude, gentleness, self-control– he’s called an elder,
dhp262:4: does an envious, miserly cheat become an exemplary man.
dhp263:1: But one in whom this is cut through
dhp263:2: up-rooted wiped out– he’s called exemplary,
dhp264:1: A shaven head doesn’t mean a contemplative. The liar observing no duties,
dhp264:4: filled with greed & desire: what kind of contemplative’s he?
dhp265:1: But whoever tunes out the dissonance of his evil qualities
dhp266:4: doesn’t mean one’s a monk. As long as one follows householders’ ways, one is no monk at all.
dhp267:2: both merit & evil and, living the chaste life,
dhp268:2: does someone confused & unknowing turn into a sage.
dhp268:3: But whoever–wise, as if holding the scales,
dhp269:2: he is a sage, that’s how he’s a sage.
dhp269:3: Whoever can weigh both sides of the world:
dhp269:4: that’s how he’s called a sage.
